newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's war on want fails to cut poverty.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's war on want fails to cut poverty.

text.p: Most Colombians live in poverty and 20 percent suffer extreme poverty despite President Ernesto Samper's pledge to improve living standards, a government official said on Wednesday.
One of the cornerstones of Samper's 1994 election platform was the so-called "Social Leap Forward", which aimed to boost the living standards of this Andean nation's 35 million inhabitants.

Cecilia Lopez, head of the National Planning Department, said social spending had grown to about 14.6 percent of gross domestic product. But she conceded that the social development programme would only achieve about 60 percent of its original aims by the end of this year -- less than eight months before Samper leaves office.
"I wouldn't say the Social Leap Forward has failed...We're starting off from a critical social situation," Lopez told a news conference.
"If these programmes had been carried out 20 years ago we would not have so many people living below the poverty line and would probably have much lower levels of violence," she added.

Colombia has the highest murder rate in Latin America -- more than 88 murders per 100,000 population, according to a recent World Bank study. It also has the highest kidnap rate in the world and is home to Latin America's longest-running guerrilla war.
Lopez said the number of Colombians living in poverty remained at the same level as in recent years, 55 percent, and blamed much of the situation on sluggish economic growth last year.
